notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1. bb2 is kept because the parts list asks for 2 mini breadboards.

Fix for bb2 having no connection: the tutorial lists one mini breadboard per board, so each board is taken to sit on its own mini breadboard (nano1 on bb1, nano2 on bb2). These are plain contact edges with no ports and no electrical edge. The circuit image draws the boards with wires going straight to their pins, so no board pin is modelled as sitting in a breadboard hole. This is an assumption.
Both boards use catalogue type arduino-nano-33-ble because it exposes A4/A5, 3V3 and GND1. The reader is the Nano 33 BLE Sense and the writer is a Nano 33 BLE. The I2C bus is SDA on A4 and SCL on A5.

As in the image, the two bus lines (A5 = SCL, A4 = SDA) join the two boards. Each line has a 4.7k pull-up to the 3V line. These are built on bb1: SCL strip 5t, SDA strip 8t, 3V3 rail tp.1 to tp.3 (one rail strip). The 3V3 comes only from the reader. The exact hole positions are my choice.
GND is a direct jumper (wire1) between the GND1 pins of the two boards.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB (usb1, usb2). These have only a joined edge, since the USB cable's ports are not modelled.
Only 6 jumper wires are used, as the image shows. The parts list's 10 is a pack quantity.
